**1. Contract Renewal Process – Standard Operating Procedure Update**

Following the review of our current contract management practices, I am issuing the following clarifications to the renewal process for all service contracts managed by LFSC. These steps take effect immediately and apply to all renewals scheduled between 2025-04-01 and 2025-09-30.

The renewal window for any contract shall be opened no earlier than 90 days before the contract expiry date. The Procurement Team is responsible for initiating the renewal checklist and circulating it to the relevant unit head. The checklist must include the following items:

- Confirmation of the current contract start date and expiry date from the LFSC contract registry.
- A review of the vendor's performance over the current term, including any service complaints logged with the LFSC Forum moderation team.
- A cost comparison against at least two alternative vendors, unless a sole-source justification has been approved by the Finance Committee.
- A written recommendation from the unit head, to be submitted to the Procurement Team no later than 30 days before the expiry date.

Once the checklist is complete, the Procurement Team will prepare a renewal summary for my review. The summary must include the proposed renewal terms, any negotiated changes, and a risk assessment. No renewal is to be executed without my signed approval on the final summary.

- The vendor has maintained consistent opening hours during the weekday service period.
- Complaints regarding food variety have decreased since Q3 2024.
- The vendor has requested a meeting to discuss a possible renewal term extension beyond the current expiry.

The Operations Unit has been asked to provide a formal performance scorecard by 2025-03-14. This scorecard will be attached to the renewal summary when it is submitted for approval.

**3. Reminder – Contract Documentation Standards**

All staff involved in contract management are reminded of the documentation requirements set out in LFSC-2024-011. The following standards apply to both new contracts and renewals:

- Every contract must have a signed original copy held in the central registry, not only in the unit office.

**1. New Moderation Guidelines – Effective 2025-03-01**

The Management of LFSC has approved a revised set of moderation guidelines for all official LFSC online platforms, including the staff forum, the public feedback portal, and the LFSC community WhatsApp group. These guidelines replace the previous moderation policy issued on 2024-08-19 and take effect on 2025-03-01.

The full text of the new guidelines is attached to this memo as Annex A. The key changes are summarised below:

- **Post Approval:** All posts by new members (accounts created less than 30 days prior) must be approved by a moderator before they appear publicly. This applies to the staff forum and the public feedback portal.
- **Language and Tone:** Posts containing abusive language, personal attacks, or hate speech will be removed immediately and the author issued a formal warning. A second offence results in a 14-day suspension from the platform concerned.
- **Commercial Content:** Advertising or promotion of personal businesses, goods, or services is prohibited on all LFSC platforms unless prior written permission has been obtained from the Communications Unit. This includes posts offering catering services, equipment sales, or recruitment agency services.
- **Confidential Information:** Staff are reminded that sharing internal LFSC documents, financial data, or personal data of clients or staff on any online platform is a serious breach of the LFSC Data Protection Policy (see LFSC-2022-112). Such posts will be removed and the matter referred to the Compliance Unit.
- **Moderator Authority:** Moderators have the authority to edit, lock, or remove any post that violates these guidelines. They are also empowered to issue warnings and temporary suspensions. Appeals against moderator decisions should be sent to the Director's Office via the official LFSC email address within 7 days of the decision.

All current moderators are required to attend a refresher training session on the new guidelines. The training will hold on 2025-02-20 from 10:00 to 13:00 in the Conference Room. Unit heads are requested to release nominated moderators for this session.

Questions about the new guidelines should be directed to the Communications Unit (Mr. T. Adeyemi, ext. 208).

These reminders are aligned with the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) guidelines and Lagos State environmental health regulations.

**Personal Hygiene:**
- All food handlers must wash hands thoroughly with soap and clean running water before handling food, after using the restroom, and after touching raw materials.
- Hairnets, beard covers, and clean aprons are mandatory in all food preparation areas.
- Remove all jewellery (rings, bracelets, watches) before starting work.
- Report any symptoms of illness (vomiting, diarrhoea, fever, jaundice) to your supervisor immediately. Do not handle food while symptomatic.

**Food Storage & Temperature Control:**
- Perishable items must be stored at or below **5°C** in refrigerators and at **-18°C** or lower in freezers.
- Hot food must be held at **63°C or above**; cold food at **8°C or below**.
- Label all stored food with the date of preparation and use-by date. Discard any item that exceeds its safe storage period.

**1. Contract Renewal Process – Standard Operating Procedure Update**

Following the review of our current contract management practices, I am issuing the following clarifications to the renewal process for all service contracts managed by LFSC. These steps take effect immediately and apply to all renewals scheduled between 2025-04-01 and 2025-09-30.

The renewal window for any contract shall be opened no earlier than 90 days before the contract expiry date. The Procurement Team is responsible for initiating the renewal checklist and circulating it to the relevant unit head. The checklist must include the following items:

- Confirmation of the current contract start date and expiry date from the LFSC contract registry.
- A review of the vendor's performance over the current term, including any service complaints logged with the LFSC Forum moderation team.
- A cost comparison against at least two alternative vendors, unless a sole-source justification has been approved by the Finance Committee.
- A written recommendation from the unit head, to be submitted to the Procurement Team no later than 30 days before the expiry date.

Once the checklist is complete, the Procurement Team will prepare a renewal summary for my review. The summary must include the proposed renewal terms, any negotiated changes, and a risk assessment. No renewal is to be executed without my signed approval on the final summary.

In line with the above, I have received the preliminary evaluation notes for the Yaba Tech Hub (YTH) cafeteria service contract. All staff involved in contract management are reminded of the documentation requirements set out in LFSC-2024-011. The following standards apply to both new contracts and renewals:

- Every contract must have a signed original copy held in the central registry, not only in the unit office.

---

**1. Compliance Training – Mandatory Attendance**

Following the appointment of Adebayo Ogunlesi as Compliance Officer with effect from 2022-08-01, all staff are required to complete the annual compliance training module. This training is a condition of continued employment and must be completed by 2022-09-30.

The training will be delivered in two formats:

- **Online Module:** Available on the LFSC staff portal from 2022-08-15. Each staff member must complete the module and submit the end-of-module assessment. A pass mark of 80% is required.
- **Physical Sessions:** Two facilitator-led sessions will be held in the main conference room:
  - Session 1: 2022-08-24, 10:00 – 12:00 WAT
  - Session 2: 2022-08-31, 14:00 – 16:00 WAT

Department heads are to ensure that all staff under their supervision are registered for one of the physical sessions or have confirmed access to the online module. A consolidated attendance list should be forwarded to the Compliance Unit by 2022-08-19.

Mr. Ogunlesi will coordinate the training logistics and will provide a summary report to the Executive Director’s office by 2022-10-07. Any staff member who does not complete the training by the deadline will be required to attend a remedial session, and their supervisor will be notified.

---

**2. Data Protection Reminder – Handling of Personal Information**

This memo serves as a reminder of the data protection obligations that apply to all LFSC staff, particularly those who handle personal data as part of their daily duties. The following points are to be observed:

- Personal data may only be collected for specified, explicit, and legitimate purposes. Staff should not request or record more information than is necessary for the task at hand.
- All personal data must be stored securely. Paper records are to be kept in locked cabinets within the relevant unit office, and digital records must be saved on the shared drive under the folder “Data – Restricted”. Do not save personal data to local desktops, personal devices, or unapproved cloud services.
- Sharing personal data with third parties is prohibited unless prior written approval has been obtained from the Compliance Officer. This includes sharing data with other government agencies, vendors, or partner organisations.
- Any suspected data breach, including loss, theft, or unauthorised access to personal data, must be reported to the Compliance Unit within 24 hours of becoming aware of the incident. The report should include the date and time of the incident, the type of data involved, and the number of individuals affected.

The Compliance Unit will conduct spot checks on data handling practices during the period 2022-09-05 to 2022-09-16. Unit heads are advised to review their current practices and correct any non-compliance before this date.

---

**3. Note on Upcoming Audit – Internal Audit Scheduled for October**

The annual internal audit is scheduled to commence on 2022-10-03. The audit will cover the period from January 2022 to September 2022. All units are required to prepare the following documents for review:

- Financial records, including receipts, payment vouchers, and bank statements.
- Procurement files, including quotations, bid evaluations, and purchase orders.
- Contract files, including signed originals and any amendments.
- Staff attendance and leave records.
- Asset register and movement logs.

- **Moderator Authority:** Moderators have the authority to edit, lock, or remove any post that violates these guidelines. They are also empowered to issue warnings and temporary suspensions. To avoid unexpected breakdowns during the peak season, we have released the following preventive maintenance schedule for all kitchen equipment supplied or serviced by NaijaKitchen Supplies. **3. HYGIENE STANDARDS REMINDER – FOOD SAFETY & HANDLING**

Following the quarterly inspection by the Lagos State Consumer Protection Agency (LASCOPA) in March 2025, we are reinforcing the following hygiene standards across all client kitchens and NKS facilities. These reminders are aligned with the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) guidelines and Lagos State environmental health regulations.

**Personal Hygiene:**
- All food handlers must wash hands thoroughly with soap and clean running water before handling food, after using the restroom, and after touching raw materials.
- Hairnets, beard covers, and clean aprons are mandatory in all food preparation areas.
- Remove all jewellery (rings, bracelets, watches) before starting work.
- Report any symptoms of illness (vomiting, diarrhoea, fever, jaundice) to your supervisor immediately. Do not handle food while symptomatic.

**Food Storage & Temperature Control:**
- Perishable items must be stored at or below **5°C** in refrigerators and at **-18°C** or lower in freezers.
- Hot food must be held at **63°C or above**; cold food at **8°C or below**.
- Label all stored food with the date of preparation and use-by date. Discard any item that exceeds its safe storage period.
- Never store raw meat, poultry, or seafood above ready-to-eat food in refrigerators to prevent cross-contamination.

**3. Quality Standards – Produce Acceptance Criteria**

Effective immediately, the following acceptance standards apply to all produce received at your premises. These standards are in line with NAFDAC guidance for fresh produce handling and our own receiving protocols.

| Leafy greens | Fresh, crisp leaves, no yellowing | Wilting, yellowing, slimy texture, or foreign matter |
| Potatoes | Clean, firm, no green patches | Green skin, sprouting, soft spots, or soil contamination |

**Sampling Note:** Receiving staff should inspect at least 10% of each delivery, taken from different parts of the crate or bag. If more than 5% of the sampled units fail the acceptance criteria, the entire delivery may be rejected or subject to a price adjustment at your discretion.

| SPM-213 | Frozen Beef Tripe (Shaki) | 5 kg pack | 13,000 | Pre-cleaned and parboiled |
| SPM-214 | Frozen Mackerel (Titus) | 10 kg carton | 21,500 | Whole fish, size 6–8 per carton |

**Seasonal Note:** Due to the current heat, we advise that all fresh produce orders be scheduled for morning delivery slots (see Section 3). We will not accept returns on perishable items unless the product is spoiled at the point of delivery, and this must be reported within 24 hours.

---

**2. STORAGE GUIDELINES – REVISED FOR FEBRUARY**

We have reviewed our storage recommendations in light of the current weather conditions and updated the following guidelines. These supersede the guidance printed in Bulletin NKS-B-2024-11.

**2.1 Fresh Produce**

- **Ugu and Scent Leaf:** Remove from the crate immediately upon delivery. Wrap the stems in a damp cloth and store upright in a refrigerator at 4–8°C. Use within 3 days. Do not store in an airtight plastic bag for more than a few hours, as condensation will cause the leaves to rot.
- **Bitter Leaf:** Keep in the original bag, loosely tied, in the refrigerator crisper drawer. Use within 5 days of delivery.
- **Watermelon:** Whole fruits can be kept at room temperature (25–30°C) for up to 5 days. Once cut, wrap tightly and refrigerate; consume within 2 days.
- **Bell Peppers:** Store in a perforated plastic bag in the refrigerator. Do not wash until ready to use. Use within 7 days.

**2.2 Frozen and Chilled Items**

- **Frozen Chicken, Tripe, and Mackerel:** Keep at -18°C or below. If you plan to use within 48 hours, you may thaw in the refrigerator (not at room temperature). Once thawed, do not refreeze.
- **Fresh Catfish:** Store on crushed ice in a perforated tray in the refrigerator (0–4°C). Use within 24 hours of delivery for best quality.
- **Smoked Catfish:** Keep in a cool, dry place in the vacuum pack. Once opened, refrigerate and use within 7 days.

**BULLETIN NKS-B-2026-01**
**Training, Certification & Audit Readiness – First Quarter 2026**

Dear Valued Client,

Welcome to 2026. We begin the year with a strong focus on helping you keep your kitchen teams skilled, certified, and audit-ready. This bulletin covers three areas that we have been receiving many questions about: (1) our upcoming practical training workshops, (2) the updated food handling certification requirements from the Lagos State Food Safety and Hygiene Committee (LSFSHC), and (3) a reminder about the supplier audit schedule for the quarter.

Please take note of the effective dates and deadlines. Where a date is marked "tentative," we will confirm by SMS and email at least one week before the event.

---

**1. PRACTICAL TRAINING WORKSHOPS – FEBRUARY 2026**

Following the success of our December workshops, we have scheduled four sessions for February. All workshops hold at our VI training kitchen (same building as our office, ground floor). Class size is limited to 12 participants per session to ensure hands-on practice.

| Course Code | Course Title | Date | Time | Fee (NGN) | Remarks |

| TR-221 | Basic Food Hygiene & Personal Hygiene | Tue, 10 Feb 2026 | 9:00 AM – 1:00 PM | 18,500 | Includes certificate |

**How to register:** Send the course code and the names of your participants to training@naijakitchensupplies.com.ng. Payment confirms your seat. The deadline for registration is **Friday, 6 February 2026, 5:00 PM**. We cannot hold seats without payment.

**Note on TR-222:** This course is especially relevant given the revised storage guidelines we issued in Bulletin NKS-B-2025-12. We will be demonstrating proper thawing procedures and temperature logging using the equipment most small restaurants in Lagos typically have. Please bring your own digital probe thermometer if you have one; we will have a few spares to lend.

---

**2. FOOD HANDLING CERTIFICATION – UPDATED REQUIREMENTS**

We have received the latest guidance from the LSFSHC, effective **1 March 2026**. The key change concerns the validity period of the Basic Food Hygiene Certificate.

- The standard certificate issued after completing a one-day course is now valid for **two (2) years** from the date of issue. Previously, the validity was one year. This change applies to all certificates issued on or after 1 March 2026.
- Certificates issued before 1 March 2026 remain valid for one year from their issue date. If your staff hold an older certificate, please check the expiry date and plan for renewal accordingly.
- **Important:** The LSFSHC has clarified that the certificate must be renewed **before** expiry. There is no grace period. If your certificate lapses, you will need to retake the full one-day course; no refresher option is available for lapsed certificates.

We will be running an extra session of TR-221 on **Saturday, 28 February 2026** specifically for those who need to renew before the new rules fully kick in. The fee for this session is the same as listed above. Please indicate "RENEWAL" in your registration email so we can prepare the correct paperwork.
